note: The target products' real chrome, in their own token names, for both modes. This is the independent reference the colour layers in tools/compare/color-parity.mjs score against — not the applied skin's own --gs-* variables — so a score measures fidelity to the product rather than self-consistency. A value marked `measured` was read out of the committed screenshot in docs/ by the same code that scores the skins, so it is the product's rendered value and not a claim about it; the `reference` layer re-checks every `measured` value on every run, and a product that moves fails there instead of quietly lowering everyone's score. Update a value (and its `asOf`) when a product's design system moves, and say where it came from.

jnd.note: ΔE in OKLab, per axis, not one combined cutoff — see TOLERANCE in tools/compare/color-parity.mjs for why a single threshold cannot separate a wrong surface from a wrong brand hue, and for the calibration these numbers come from. A colour over any axis is out of tolerance and fails. They are recorded here as well as in the module so a reviewer reading only the fixture can see what 'a match' means.

github.provenance: Primer (github/primer) for the ramps; the header surface is `measured` — Primer's published header token no longer describes what github.com serves. Dark values are from the design system: the committed captures are light-mode only, so nothing dark is measured here.
github.compareOnNote: Only the GitLab source. The GitHub skin rebuilds GitLab's super-sidebar as GitHub's horizontal tab row, so a region-for-region compare means the same thing on both sides. Gitea's own light header and PolyGerrit's shell are left as they are — measuring those against github.com's black bar would be measuring the source's layout, which the UX rubric already accounts for through each source's `compare` capabilities.

header.note: The dark application bar above the repo header. `measured`: the capture is #000000 across this box at 96%, so the skin's #25292e is a stale Primer token, not a product value.

tabs.note: The repository tab row, which GitHub paints canvas-subtle rather than canvas. `measured`: #f6f8fa at 89%.

gitlab.provenance: Pajamas (gitlab-org/gitlab-svgs / the Pajamas design tokens) for the ramps; the header and the navigation rail are `measured` — GitLab paints both with its gray-100, #ececef, which is the colour the product uses for the rail and not a distinct header surface. Dark values are from the design system: the committed captures are light-mode only.
gitlab.compareOnNote: Only the GitHub source, for the same reason: the GitLab skin rebuilds GitHub's UnderlineNav as GitLab's own grouped sidebar, so both sides of a region are laid out the product's way. Gitea is a full rebuild too and would be comparable, but its capture is a different repository on a different design system, so it is left to the UX rubric rather than read as a colour-fidelity number here.

header.note: The super-topbar, which starts at x=240 beside the rail. `measured`: #ececef at 63%, and it is the same gray the rail uses — so the reference is canvas-inset, not a separate header value.

rail.note: The project navigation rail, GitLab's most recognisable layout cue: a gray column against a white content canvas. `measured`: #ececef at 80%.

bitbucket.provenance: Atlassian design tokens (--ds-*) for the ramps. The header is the archived bitbucket.org theme-color, which the live product no longer serves, so it is the one value here that is neither measured nor current — see `docs/LIMITATIONS.md`. Bitbucket has no `header` region: the committed capture is of a 2024 archived repository and its top ~100px is a cookie banner, so nothing in it is the application bar and there is nothing honest to measure.
bitbucket.compareOnNote: No comparable skinned capture. Bitbucket is a target only and is applied as a palette over a source's own chrome — it never rebuilds a layout — and the one committed Bitbucket capture is of a 2024 archived repository whose top ~100px is a cookie banner, so the regions below it do not line up with a capture that has no banner. The `tokens` layer is the meaningful one for this skin; the `pixels` layer reports n/a rather than a number that would mean nothing.

rail.note: Below the cookie banner. `measured`: #ffffff at 93% — live Bitbucket Cloud is white-on-white, with no tinted rail.
